# metric-against-trivial-predictor

**Claim.** Never report a model metric without the score a trivial predictor gets on the same data, and never read a delta smaller than run-to-run noise as a result.

**Not when.** Balanced labels, where standard metrics are already informative (the extra row is usually kept anyway)

**Check.** every metric table has the trivial-predictor row and an interval; each new label's base rate is asserted

*measured.* Open the full note only when you cannot tell whether its boundary holds here: [metric-against-trivial-predictor](../notes/active/metric-against-trivial-predictor.md).
